variables.label: Tropospheric NO2 Column (OMNO2d v004)
variables.plain_definition: Satellite-measured nitrogen dioxide (NO2) gas density in the tropospheric (lower-atmosphere) air column above the study box, reflecting fuel combustion from traffic, power generation, and industry.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.25 deg OMI grid averaged over Kyiv 0.5 deg box
spatial_support.sampling_method: Area mean across snapped 0.25 deg pixel centers inside Kyiv box (30.273-30.773E, 50.2-50.7N)

sources: NASA Aura OMI OMNO2d v004 via Giovanni
limitations: Only Kyiv study box has NO2 retrievals in this archive; not a city street-level map.
April 2022 has low valid retrieval coverage (8/30 days; 26.7%) due to cloud cover.
Observed 2022 drop reflects combined weather ventilation and emission shifts; single-season record does not establish war causation.

variables.label: 10m Wind Speed
variables.plain_definition: Average wind speed measured 10 meters above ground, controlling how quickly air pollution is blown away and dispersed.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Coarse 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg reanalysis regional context; cannot resolve urban canyon wind dispersion.
Used as an atmospheric-ventilation confounder check alongside OMI NO2, not as war-damage evidence.

variables.label: Total Cloud Amount
variables.plain_definition: Percentage of the sky covered by clouds, which cools daytime surfaces and causes missing days in satellite NO2 observations.

spatial_support.resolution: 1.0 deg CERES sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Coarse 1.0 deg regional box average explaining OMI cloud screening gaps (e.g., April 2022).
Represents synoptic cloudiness context rather than direct anthropogenic plumes.

variables.label: Surface Barometric Pressure
variables.plain_definition: Air pressure at the ground surface, tracking passing high-pressure fair weather versus low-pressure storm systems (levels also vary with ground elevation).

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Regional synoptic pressure context only; small relative % fluctuations reflect atmospheric pressure baselines (~99 kPa).

variables.label: Clear-Sky Downward Shortwave Radiation
variables.plain_definition: Incoming sunlight energy on a cloudless day, set mainly by season, latitude, and atmospheric haze as the clear-sky solar ceiling.

spatial_support.resolution: 1.0 deg CERES sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Clear-sky radiative baseline from 1.0 deg CERES model estimates; does not directly isolate localized smoke aerosols.

variables.label: Cloud-Related Sunlight Reduction (SWclr - SWall)
variables.plain_definition: Average sunlight power blocked or reflected by clouds before reaching the ground (clear-sky minus all-sky solar radiation, converted to W/m^2).

spatial_support.resolution: 1.0 deg CERES difference derived over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: (CLRSKY_SFC_SW_DWN - ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN) * 1e6 / 86400

uncertainty_and_status.pct_change_withheld_reason: Interval-scale or signed quantity crossing zero; report abs_diff instead of % change.

limitations: Derived signed radiative difference (W/m^2); relative % change is strictly withheld as non-meaningful across near-zero values.
Coarse 1.0 deg context only; cannot isolate local dust/smoke plumes from clouds.

variables.label: VIIRS Presumed Vegetation Fire Density (type 0)
variables.plain_definition: Number of satellite-detected vegetation fire hotspots (nominal/high confidence) per 1,000 square kilometers per satellite-observed day; counts pixel hotspots across overpasses, not distinct fires or burned area.

supported_baselines.label: 2015–2019
supported_baselines.unsupported_reason: VIIRS S-NPP Archive Export in this repository starts in 2019-03; 2015-2018 data is absent so 2015-2019 baseline must stay disabled.

spatial_support.resolution: 375 m VIIRS S-NPP pixels summarized over study boxes and 0.25 deg grid cells
spatial_support.sampling_method: Type-0 detection count divided by (box_area_km2 / 1000) and CMR VNP14IMG observed satellite days

sources: NASA FIRMS VIIRS S-NPP Archive Export (SV-C2)
limitations: 2015-2019 baseline is strictly unsupported/disabled because this archive begins in 2019-03 (only 2019-2021 pre-war baseline is valid).
Hotspot pixel counts are not burned area in km^2: repeated overpasses and multi-pixel fire fronts cluster detections (~1.42 det/cell-day).
2022 contains a 16-day satellite observation gap (notably 2022-07-27 through 2022-08-10 orbit outage, plus 2022-03-05).
Matched-date (169d/yr) UKR-ADM0 polygon clipping shifts absolute ratios (~63.9% vs 104.3% in Donbas) and is kept strictly separate.

variables.label: VIIRS Other Static Land Source Density (type 2)
variables.plain_definition: Number of persistent stationary heat detections (steelworks, industrial plants, and gas flares) per 1,000 square kilometers per satellite-observed day.

supported_baselines.label: 2015–2019
supported_baselines.unsupported_reason: VIIRS S-NPP Archive Export in this repository starts in 2019-03; 2015-2018 data is absent so 2015-2019 baseline must stay disabled.

spatial_support.resolution: 375 m VIIRS S-NPP pixels summarized over study boxes and 0.25 deg grid cells
spatial_support.sampling_method: Type-2 static land source count divided by (box_area_km2 / 1000) and CMR VNP14IMG observed satellite days

sources: NASA FIRMS VIIRS S-NPP Archive Export (SV-C2)
limitations: 2015-2019 baseline is strictly unsupported/disabled (archive begins 2019-03).
Tracks stationary industrial/metallurgical/gas-flare hotspots; sharp 2022 drops in frontline corridors (e.g. -83% in Donbas-Kharkiv) reflect facility shutdowns/destruction rather than fire absence.
Boxes with zero baseline type-2 detections (e.g. Kyiv 0.5 deg box) withhold % change.

variables.label: 2m Air Temperature
variables.plain_definition: Monthly average air temperature 2 meters above the ground, describing regional baseline warmth across seasons.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

uncertainty_and_status.pct_change_withheld_reason: Interval-scale or signed quantity crossing zero; report abs_diff instead of % change.

limitations: Interval-scale °C unit: absolute difference is reported while relative % change is strictly withheld (null).
Regional fire-weather context only (0.5 deg box average), not local flame temperature.

variables.label: Monthly Peak 2m Air Temperature (T2M_MAX)
variables.plain_definition: Monthly extreme maximum air temperature at 2 meters height (single hottest reading of the month, not the mean of daily highs), capturing heat extremes that dry surface fuels.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of monthly extreme maximum 2m air temperature (T2M_MAX)

uncertainty_and_status.pct_change_withheld_reason: Interval-scale or signed quantity crossing zero; report abs_diff instead of % change.

limitations: Interval-scale °C unit: relative % change is strictly withheld (null).
Coarse 0.5 deg box average cannot capture fine-scale heat domes.

variables.label: Diurnal Temperature Range (T2M_RANGE)
variables.plain_definition: Monthly average of the daily spread between daytime high and nighttime low temperatures, which widens during sunny dry spells and shrinks under clouds.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of daily Tmax - Tmin magnitude

limitations: Regional synoptic dryness/clear-sky context indicator; coarse 0.5 deg resolution.

variables.label: All-Sky Downward Shortwave Sunlight
variables.plain_definition: Actual average solar energy reaching the ground after cloud shading, driving surface heating and water evaporation.

spatial_support.resolution: 1.0 deg CERES sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Coarse 1.0 deg surface insolation context used in radiation/PET fire-weather checks.

variables.label: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith Potential Evapotranspiration (PET)
variables.plain_definition: Standardized FAO-56 Penman-Monteith evaporation demand from a hypothetical well-watered reference grass surface given local sun, heat, humidity, and wind.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg MERRA-2 / 1.0 deg CERES derived over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Monthly FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference ET using regional box elevation; strict daily PM sensitivity checked (RMSE 0.119 mm/day)

limitations: Measures atmospheric evaporative demand over coarse regional boxes, not actual irrigation or localized drought stress.

variables.label: Bias-Corrected Total Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR)
variables.plain_definition: Bias-corrected total precipitation (rain and melted snowfall) reaching the land surface as millimeters of liquid water per day across the study box.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Regional 0.5 deg environmental context ONLY: averages smooth localized storm deficits and do NOT rule out sub-regional or short-term drought.
Does not measure reservoir levels, drinking-water infrastructure damage, or contamination.

variables.label: Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD)
variables.plain_definition: Atmospheric drying pull (vapor pressure deficit): gap between saturation vapor pressure at air temperature and actual vapor pressure, showing how strongly dry air draws moisture.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 derived over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: e_s(T2M) * (1 - RH2M / 100) using Tetens saturation vapor pressure formula

limitations: Regional atmospheric drying-demand context only; coarse 0.5 deg boxes cannot produce local drought heatmaps or rule out local soil/water stress.

variables.label: 2m Specific Humidity
variables.plain_definition: Actual mass of water vapor mixed into every kilogram of moist near-surface air, measuring true atmospheric moisture content.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Coarse 0.5 deg regional moisture context only; not direct hydrological damage evidence.

variables.label: 2m Relative Humidity
variables.plain_definition: Percentage of water vapor the air holds compared with the maximum it could hold at its current temperature.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Coarse 0.5 deg regional atmospheric humidity context only; cannot substitute for catchment drought or water quality data.

variables.label: Vegetation Transpiration Flux (EVPTRNS)
variables.plain_definition: Model-estimated daily water transpired by vegetation canopies through leaves into the atmosphere (MERRA-2 transpiration energy flux converted via temperature-dependent latent heat).

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean converted from MJ/m^2/day transpiration energy flux via Bolton lambda(T) = max(2.2, 2.501 - 0.002361 * T2M) MJ/kg

limitations: Reanalysis land-surface model estimate at 0.5 deg resolution; does not directly observe field-scale crop stress or destroyed irrigation.

variables.label: Climatic Water Balance (Rainfall minus PET)
variables.plain_definition: Climatic water balance (total precipitation minus FAO-56 reference evaporation demand): positive indicates moisture surplus and negative indicates net drying pressure.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg MERRA-2 / 1.0 deg CERES derived over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: PRECTOTCORR - PET_FAO56 in mm/day

uncertainty_and_status.pct_change_withheld_reason: Interval-scale or signed quantity crossing zero; report abs_diff instead of % change.

limitations: Signed interval difference crossing zero: relative % change is strictly withheld (null); inspect abs_diff (mm/day) instead.
Coarse regional context only; does not rule out localized seasonal drought or measure water-system damage.

variables.label: Surface Soil Wetness (0-5 cm, GWETTOP)
variables.plain_definition: MERRA-2 modeled moisture saturation in the top 5 cm of soil (from 0 completely water-free to 1 fully saturated).

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Regional 0.5 deg environmental context ONLY: broad box means do not rule out localized drought and do NOT directly observe cratering, landmines, or soil contamination.

variables.label: Root-Zone Soil Wetness (0-100 cm, GWETROOT)
variables.plain_definition: MERRA-2 modeled moisture saturation across the 0-1 m plant root zone (from 0 water-free to 1 fully saturated), tracking crop water reserves.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: 0.5 deg reanalysis soil moisture context; cannot resolve farm-level soil disruption or war land degradation.

variables.label: Full-Profile Soil Wetness (GWETPROF)
variables.plain_definition: MERRA-2 modeled water saturation across the full vertical soil column to bedrock, changing more slowly across seasons than surface soil.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: 0.5 deg deep soil moisture context; seasonal box means do not establish or rule out localized agricultural stress.

variables.label: Earth Skin Surface Temperature (TS)
variables.plain_definition: Modeled radiometric skin temperature of the ground surface itself, rising relative to air temperature when soils dry out.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

uncertainty_and_status.pct_change_withheld_reason: Interval-scale or signed quantity crossing zero; report abs_diff instead of % change.

limitations: Interval-scale °C unit: relative % change is strictly withheld (null); use abs_diff (°C).
Coarse 0.5 deg thermal context only; cannot produce sub-kilometer land-surface temperature heatmaps.

variables.label: Surface-minus-Air Temperature Difference (Ts - T2m)
variables.plain_definition: 24-hour monthly mean temperature difference between the modeled ground skin and air 2 meters above it (-1.4 to +2.0 °C across study boxes), reflecting surface heating versus evaporative cooling.

spatial_support.resolution: 0.5 deg x 0.625 deg MERRA-2 derived over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: TS - T2M in °C

uncertainty_and_status.pct_change_withheld_reason: Interval-scale or signed quantity crossing zero; report abs_diff instead of % change.

limitations: Signed difference near zero: relative % change is strictly withheld (null).
Coarse regional surface-energy context only.

variables.label: All-Sky Surface Albedo
variables.plain_definition: Fraction of incoming sunlight reflected off the land surface back into space, varying with winter snow, bare soil, and crop greenness.

spatial_support.resolution: 1.0 deg CERES sampled over 3x3 cos(lat) lattice
spatial_support.sampling_method: Cos(lat)-weighted mean of 3x3 box-spanning NASA POWER grid points

limitations: Coarse 1.0 deg surface reflectance indicator; snow cover, cloudiness, and regional crop phenology dominate box averages.

properties.name: East Frontline Corridor (Donbas–Kharkiv, proposed study)
properties.description: Proposed active-conflict eastern belt spanning Kharkiv, Luhansk, Donetsk, and eastern Zaporizhzhia.

properties.name: South Steppe Corridor (Kherson–Mykolaiv–Crimea edge, proposed study)
properties.description: Proposed southern steppe and coastal frontline corridor west of 35.5E.

properties.name: North Corridor (Kyiv–Chernihiv belt, proposed study)
properties.description: Proposed northern forest/agricultural corridor covering Kyiv and Chernihiv oblasts (February–March invasion axis).

properties.name: Kyiv Air-Matched Box (0.5 deg, cross-layer check)
properties.description: Exact bounding box used in the Air/NO2 OMNO2d analysis for Kyiv cross-element context.

properties.name: Central Interior Steppe (proposed reference for East/South)
properties.description: Proposed lower-ground-combat central agricultural/steppe comparator matched by climate belt to East/South.

properties.name: Western Ukraine (proposed reference for North/Kyiv)
properties.description: Proposed western lower-ground-combat comparator matched by spring fire seasonality to Kyiv/North.

properties.name: Krakow Box (Poland, meteorological context)
properties.description: 0.5 deg external EU reference city box for synoptic climate comparison.

properties.name: Prague Box (Czechia, meteorological context)
properties.description: 0.5 deg external EU reference city box for synoptic climate comparison.

global_limitations: Regional MERRA-2 (0.5 deg x 0.625 deg) and CERES (1.0 deg) box means describe synoptic environmental context, cannot generate local pollution/drought heatmaps, and do not rule out localized drought or prove war-caused damage.
Fire hotspot counts are satellite thermal pixel detections (type 0 vs type 2), not burned area in km^2; 2015-2019 baseline is unavailable and must stay disabled.
Single-season 2022 before-after comparisons are descriptive and cannot isolate causal war attribution without validated counterfactuals.
